packages.title: UK PRTR 2024 dataset vintage QA
facts: Defra published the downloadable 2024 UK Pollutant Release and Transfer Register dataset on 30 June 2026.
The dataset is an annual industrial emissions and waste-transfer register.
Reporting year and publication date are distinct fields and must both be preserved.
A national PRTR download can contain many facilities and pollutants.
No parcel value is inferred solely from dataset inclusion.

packages.title: UK PRTR air-water-soil media QA
facts: UK PRTR records pollutant releases to air, water and soil within its reporting framework.
Environmental media are separate reporting categories.
A pollutant release to one medium must not be relabelled as a release to another.
PRTR pollutant releases are not automatically greenhouse-gas totals.
No parcel GHG value is inferred from a media category.

packages.title: UK PRTR off-site transfer QA
facts: UK PRTR also includes off-site transfers for treatment or disposal within its reporting framework.
A transfer is movement of pollutant or waste away from a site, not necessarily an on-site release.
Release and transfer fields must remain distinct.
Transferred waste mass must not be treated as emitted GHG mass.
No parcel emissions are inferred from transfer records alone.

packages.title: UK PRTR method-code QA
facts: PRTR guidance distinguishes estimated, measured and calculated reporting methods through method codes.
Method provenance is necessary when comparing facility records.
Estimated and measured values must not be treated as equivalent evidence types.
A method code describes how a reported release value was derived.
No precision beyond the source method is added.

packages.title: UK PRTR reporting-threshold QA
facts: PRTR guidance provides pollutant and threshold information for register reporting.
A reporting threshold defines whether a release is reportable under the register rules.
Being below a threshold does not imply zero physical emissions.
Threshold presence is not an exact emissions measurement.
No parcel value is inferred from threshold status alone.

packages.title: UK PRTR facility versus parcel QA
facts: PRTR is organised around industrial sites or facilities and relevant reporting activities.
A facility boundary is not automatically identical to a cadastral parcel boundary.
Facility records require verified spatial identifiers before any parcel join.
Nearby land must not inherit a facility release value by proximity.
Parcel binding remains false in this evidence batch.

packages.title: UK PRTR system-migration QA
facts: Defra states the UK PRTR is moving to a new system and provides downloadable XML data during the move.
A delivery-system change does not by itself change the meaning of historical reporting-year values.
File format and reporting semantics must remain separate.
Migration status is source-provenance information.
No missing values are fabricated during the system transition.

packages.title: Vehicle licensing Q1 2026 769,000 new registrations QA
facts: DfT reports about 769,000 vehicles registered for the first time in the UK in 2026 Q1.
This was 5.1% higher than 2025 Q1.
New registrations are a flow over a quarter.
Vehicle-registration flow is not a GHG emissions total.
No parcel emissions are inferred from national registrations.

packages.title: Vehicle licensing Q1 2026 150,000 ZEV registrations QA
facts: DfT reports about 150,000 zero emission vehicles registered for the first time in the UK in 2026 Q1.
The year-on-year increase was 12.9% compared with 2025 Q1.
The statistic is a registration flow, not the total ZEV stock.
Registration counts are not energy consumption or GHG mass.
No parcel value is inferred from the ZEV registration count.

packages.title: Licensed ZEV stock 2.148 million QA
facts: At the end of March 2026 DfT reports about 2.148 million licensed zero emission vehicles in the UK.
This was 29.6% higher than in March 2025.
Licensed vehicles are a stock at a point in time rather than a quarterly registration flow.
Stock growth does not directly quantify vehicle kilometres or electricity use.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from the national stock.

packages.title: Licensed ZEV 5.1 percent share QA
facts: DfT reports zero emission vehicles were 5.1% of all licensed vehicles at the end of March 2026.
The percentage uses the licensed-vehicle stock as its denominator.
A stock share is not an emissions share.
The figure does not describe how far vehicles travelled.
No local emissions value is inferred from the national share.

packages.title: New zero-emission cars 21.8 percent share QA
facts: DfT reports around 138,000 zero emission cars were newly registered in 2026 Q1.
Zero emission cars accounted for 21.8% of new car registrations in that quarter.
This percentage applies to new registrations, not the full licensed car stock.
Registration share is not lifecycle GHG performance.
No parcel emissions are inferred from new-car market share.

packages.title: New zero-emission LGV 8.8 percent share QA
facts: DfT reports 7,443 road-using zero emission light goods vehicles newly registered in 2026 Q1.
They represented 8.8% of new road-using LGV registrations in the quarter.
LGV registration categories follow DfT vehicle-classification rules.
New-registration share is not fleet energy use or GHG emissions.
No parcel value is inferred from LGV registration data.

packages.title: Zero-emission vehicle tailpipe-definition QA
facts: DfT defines zero emission vehicles in this release as vehicles reported to emit 0 g CO2 from the tailpipe per kilometre, currently battery-electric and fuel-cell-electric vehicles.
The definition concerns tailpipe CO2.
It does not by itself represent lifecycle or electricity-generation emissions.
Tailpipe classification must not be relabelled as zero total GHG impact.
No parcel emissions are inferred from the vehicle technology label.

packages.title: DVLA administrative database stock-flow QA
facts: DfT vehicle licensing statistics are derived primarily from DVLA administrative registration and licensing records.
New registrations and licensed stock are different measures derived from the administrative system.
Vehicles can leave the licensed stock through SORN, scrappage, write-off or export routes.
Administrative vehicle presence does not establish usage intensity.
No parcel activity or emissions are inferred from a licensing record alone.

packages.title: England household-waste recycling 43.8 percent QA
facts: Defra reports the official England waste-from-households recycling rate was 43.8% in calendar year 2024.
Total waste from households was 21.9 million tonnes in 2024.
Waste tonnage and recycling rate are waste-management metrics rather than GHG emissions.
Calendar-year and financial-year measures must remain distinct.
No parcel emissions are inferred from national waste statistics.

packages.title: England local-authority waste incineration 50.3 percent QA
facts: Defra reports 50.3% of all local-authority waste was incinerated in England in 2024/25, about 12.7 million tonnes.
The same release reports 5.5% was sent to landfill, about 1.4 million tonnes.
Treatment-route tonnage is not the same as treatment-related GHG emissions.
The 2024/25 annual figures are final while earlier-year figures can be revised according to the source policy.
No parcel GHG value is assigned from treatment-route shares.

packages.title: Cross-source parcel inference guard 107 QA
facts: This batch combines corporate reporting rules, ETS eligibility, housing-programme activity, industrial registers, vehicle statistics and waste statistics only as QA evidence.
The sources use incompatible units, geographies, denominators and reporting boundaries.
No cross-source arithmetic is used to manufacture a parcel-level emissions value.
Facility, household, company, vehicle and local-authority records require explicit verified joins before spatial allocation.
Parcel binding confidence remains 0% and measured parcel values produced remain zero.
